questions.q_en: A body of mass 10 kg is lifted vertically upward by 2 meters. Calculate the work done against gravity. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.solution_en:
Work is done when a force causes an object to move a certain distance. In this case, the force is gravity, and the distance is the vertical displacement of the body. When lifting an object against gravity, the work done is equal to the change in its potential energy.

· Work done = Force X displacement(h)

· Force = mass(m) X acceleration due to gravity(g)

· Work done = m * g * h

· Given

o m = 10 kg

o g = 9.8 m/s²

o h = 2 meters

· Work done = 10 kg * 9.8 m/s² * 2 m = 196 Joules(J)

questions.q_en: Which of the following is NOT a unit of power?
questions.solution_en:
· Watt (W) is the standard SI unit of power.

· Joule/second (J/s) is also a unit of power. Power is defined as the rate at which work is done, and work is measured in Joules. So, Joules per second is equivalent to Watts.

· Horsepower (hp) is another unit of power, commonly used for engines.

· Newton-meter (N⋅m) is a unit of torque or moment, not power. While related to work and energy, torque describes a rotational force. Work is done by a torque, but the Newton-meter itself is the unit of torque

Match the following:

Column AColumn B
i. Kinetic Energyb.mgh
ii. Potential Energya. ½mv²
iii. Workc. F X d
iv. Powerd. Work/time

स्तंभ Aस्तंभ B
i. गतिज ऊर्जाb.mgh

iii. कार्यc. F X d

questions.solution_en:
Kinetic Energy (KE):

· Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion. The formula ½mv² calculates this energy, where:

o m = mass of the object

o velocity (speed) of the object

· A heavier object moving faster has more kinetic energy. A stationary object has zero kinetic energy.

Potential Energy (PE):

Potential energy is the energy an object possesses due to its position in a force field (like gravity). The formula mgh calculates gravitational potential energy, where:

· m = mass of the object

· g = acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth)

· h = height of the object above a reference point

· The higher an object is, the more gravitational potential energy it has. At ground level (our usual reference point), the potential energy is often considered to be zero.

Work (W):

Work is done when a force causes an object to move a certain distance. The formula F X d calculates work, where:

· F = force applied to the object

· d = distance the object moves in the direction of the force

· If you push a box across the floor, you're doing work on the box. If you push against a wall and it doesn't move, you're not doing any work (even though you're exerting a force) because the distance is zero.

Power (P):

Power is the rate at which work is done. The formula Work/time calculates power, where:

· Work = the amount of work done

· time = the time taken to do that work

· A more powerful engine can do the same amount of work (like lifting a weight) in less time than a less powerful engine. Power is measured in Watts (Joules per second).

questions.q_en: A body has 100 J of kinetic energy. If its velocity is doubled, its kinetic energy will be:
questions.solution_en:
· The formula for kinetic energy is: KE = ½ mv²

where m is mass and v is velocity

· Initially:

100 J = ½ m(v₁)²

where v₁ is the initial velocity

· When velocity is doubled:

v₂ = 2v₁ where v₂ is the new velocity

· The new kinetic energy will be: KE₂ = ½ m(v₂)² = ½ m(2v₁)² = ½ m(4v₁²) = 2mv₁²

· Since ½ mv₁² = 100 J

Therefore, KE₂ = 2(100 J) = 400 J

Also, kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity. When velocity doubles, the kinetic energy increases by a factor of 4.

questions.q_en: The gravitational potential energy of an object depends on:
questions.solution_en:
The formula for gravitational potential energy is:

PE = mgh

Where:

· PE = Gravitational Potential Energy

· m = mass of the object

· g = acceleration due to gravity (a constant value)

· h = height of the object above a reference point

As you can see from the formula, potential energy is directly proportional to both mass (m) and height (h). If either mass or height increases, the potential energy increases.

If either is zero, the potential energy is zero.

questions.q_en: When an object moves in a circular path, and the force is always perpendicular to the displacement, the work done is:
questions.solution_en:
When an object moves in a circular path, the centripetal force (the force that keeps the object moving in a circle) is always directed perpendicular to the displacement of the object at every point along the path.

Work done = F X d X cosθ

where:

· F is the force applied,

· d is the displacement,

· θ is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.

When force is perpendicular to displacement, θ = 90°. Substituting this into the formula:

cos90° = 0, therefore work done = 0.

Thus, no work is done when the force is perpendicular to the displacement, as in the case of circular motion.

questions.q_en: The principle of conservation of energy states that:
options_en: Energy can be created but not destroyed
Energy can be destroyed but not created
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
Energy can be both created and destroyed
questions.solution_en:
The principle of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another or transferred from one object to another. This is a fundamental law of physics and applies to all isolated systems.

For example:

· In a closed system, the total amount of energy remains constant over time.

· Energy can change forms (e.g., kinetic energy to potential energy, or electrical energy to heat energy), but the total energy remains the same.

questions.q_en: A simple pendulum has maximum potential energy at:
questions.solution_en:
In a simple pendulum:

· The mean position (the lowest point of the swing) is where the pendulum has maximum kinetic energy and minimum potential energy.

· The extreme positions (the highest points of the swing) are where the pendulum momentarily comes to rest. At these points, the pendulum has maximum potential energy and minimum kinetic energy (zero).

This is because:

· At the extreme positions, the pendulum is at its maximum height, and gravitational potential energy (U=mgh) is at its highest.

· As the pendulum swings back toward the mean position, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is an example of negative work?
options_en: Applying brakes to a moving car
questions.solution_en:
· Negative work occurs when the force applied to an object acts opposite to the direction of the object's motion. In the case of brakes, the force is applied to slow down the car, which is in the opposite direction of the car's forward movement. This reduces the car's kinetic energy.

Further insight:

· Lifting a book: The force you apply is upwards, and the book moves upwards. The force and displacement are in the same direction, therefore, it's positive work.

· Walking on level ground: While there are forces at play, the net work done by your body to move you forward on level ground is approximately zero. The forces of your feet pushing back and the ground pushing forward mostly cancel out in terms of displacement. There is work done to overcome friction and maintain speed, but it is not negative work.

· Pushing a wall: You apply a force to the wall, but the wall doesn't move. Since there's no displacement (distance moved), no work is done (work = force x distance). Therefore, it's neither positive nor negative work.

questions.q_en: The work done in moving a body over a closed path is:
questions.solution_en:
In a closed path, final position equals initial position. Net displacement is zero, therefore total work done is zero.

This is a fundamental concept in physics related to conservative forces. For conservative forces, the work done in moving an object between two points does not depend on the path taken. So, if the starting and ending points are the same (a closed path), the net work is always zero.

questions.q_en: The work-energy theorem states that:
options_en: Work done is equal to the change in potential energy.
Work done is equal to the change in kinetic energy.
Potential energy is equal to kinetic energy.
questions.solution_en:
The work-energy theorem states that the work done by the net force acting on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.

Mathematically, this is expressed as:

W=ΔKE

where:

· W is the work done by the net force,

· ΔKE is the change in kinetic energy (KE=1/2mv2).

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relationship between work, energy, and power?
options_en: Work represents the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy is the capacity to do work, and power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred
Power is the capacity to do work, and energy represents the rate at which work is done
Work, energy and power are same
questions.solution_en:
Energy:

o Energy is the capacity to do work.

o It exists in various forms (e.g., kinetic, potential, thermal) and can be transferred or transformed.

o The unit of energy is the joule (J).

Work:

o Work is done when a force causes a displacement.

o It is a measure of energy transfer.

o The unit of work is also the joule (J).

Power:

o Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

o It measures how quickly energy is used or transferred.

o The unit of power is the watt (W), where 1 W=1 J/s1W=1J/s.

questions.q_en: In an elastic collision:
options_en: total linear momentum is not conserved
total kinetic energy of the system is not conserved
total kinetic energy of the system is conserved
questions.solution_en:
In an elastic collision:

· Total linear momentum is conserved:

o This is true for all types of collisions, whether elastic or inelastic. Momentum conservation is a fundamental law of physics.

· Total kinetic energy of the system is conserved:

o This is the defining characteristic of an elastic collision. In such collisions, the total kinetic energy before the collision is equal to the total kinetic energy after the collision.

Examples of elastic collisions include collisions between billiard balls or gas molecules (in ideal conditions).

questions.q_en:
Below are a few statements about kinetic energy.

A. Kinetic energy depends on the mass and velocity of an object.

B. Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
options_en: Both A and B are correct
questions.solution_en:
The formula for kinetic energy is KE = (1/2)mv², where 'm' is mass and 'v' is velocity. Both mass and velocity directly affect the kinetic energy.

Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction. It's just a value representing the amount of energy associated with motion. Unlike velocity (which is a vector), kinetic energy doesn't have a directional component.

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options_en: Work done is a scalar quantity
Work done is measured in joules
Work done is a vector quantity
questions.solution_en:
Work done is a scalar quantity. It has magnitude but no direction. While the force and displacement involved in work can be vectors, their dot product (which is how work is calculated) results in a scalar value.

Work done is negative when the force and displacement are in opposite directions (e.g., friction acting against motion).

The SI unit of work is the joule (J), where 1 J=1 N⋅m

questions.q_en: An electric bulb of 60 W runs for 5 hours. The energy consumed in kWh is:
questions.solution_en:
To calculate the energy consumed by the electric bulb, use the formula:

Energy (kWh)=Power (W) X Time (h)/1000

Given:

· Power (P) = 60 W,

· Time (t) = 5 hours.

Substitute the values into the formula:

Energy=60 X 5/1000=300/1000=0.3 kWh

questions.q_en: The work done against gravity in moving a body horizontally is:
questions.solution_en:
In horizontal motion, displacement is perpendicular to gravitational force, making work done against gravity zero.

Work is done when a force causes displacement. When moving horizontally, the force of gravity acts vertically downwards. Since the displacement is perpendicular to the force of gravity, no work is done against gravity. If you were moving the object upwards against gravity, then work would be done. Horizontally, gravity doesn't contribute.

· Mathematically, average power (Pavg​) is given by:

Pavg=Wt ​

where W is the work done and t is the total time taken.

· Power is a scalar quantity, not a vector.

· Power is calculated using work (a scalar) and time (a scalar), and it has no direction associated with it.
